data.title: Duties of a Registrar
data.text:
(1) A Registrar must perform the duties required by these rules and the Court of Appeal, including, subject to any direction of the Court, (a) establishing and maintaining a court file for each appeal, (b) establishing and maintaining lists of appeals, including the Civil Appeal Hearing List, (c) receiving and filing all appeal materials, having control and custody of them, and distributing them to the judges as required, (d) attending in court as required and keeping a record of all proceed- ings before the Court and its judges, including (i) keeping records of particulars of the appeals heard and the judges in attendance, (ii) identifying the appearing parties and their counsel, (iii) keeping records of particulars of the appeal heard and the result of the appeal, and (iv) noting the time occupied in hearing, (e) keeping proper accounts of money and property received or dispersed, (f) settling and signing judgments and orders in accordance with these rules, and (g) at the conclusion of an appeal, returning to the court appealed from any records of that court.
(2) In the absence of a Registrar, a Deputy Registrar or another person appointed by the Court may act in place of the Registrar.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 14.1 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. May 31, 2021); Alta.*

commentary.text:
The Court of Appeal first considered rule 14.92(e) in Hok v. Alberta the Registrar. In that case, the Registrar had referred the appellant’s appeal of a Court of King’s Bench summary judgment that dismissed a lawsuit. The appellant was required to obtain permission to appeal that judgment for two reasons: first, although the appellant had purported to inflate the value of her claim to $600,000, the appellant’s claim was in fact for less than $25,000 (permission to appeal for claims below $25,000 is required pursuant to rule 14.5(1)(g)); second, the appellant had been ordered in a previous decision of the Court of King’s Bench not to file any material on any court file or institute or further any court proceedings, absent permission of the court. For both reasons, permission was a condition precedent to the appellant’s appeal, and the Registrar was correct in determining these matters were “significantly irregular” under rule 14.92(e).

data.title: Definitions
sentences: In this Part
(a) “existing proceeding” means a court proceeding commenced but not concluded under the former rules

(b) “former rules” means the ([Alta. Reg.] 390/68) Alberta Rules of Court in effect immediately before these rules come into force. *[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 15.1 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*

data.title: New rules apply to existing proceedings
data.text:
(1) Except as otherwise provided in an enactment, by this Part or by an order under rule 15.6 [Resolution of difficulty or doubt], these rules apply to every existing proceeding.
(2) Every order or judgment made under the former rules and everything done in the course of an existing proceeding is to be considered to have been done under these rules and has the same effect under these rules as it had under the former rules.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 15.2 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*

data.title: Filing of orders or judgments
data.text:
Where on the coming into force of these rules a person has not filed an order or judgment that the person was required to file under the former rules, the person must file the order or judgment within (a) one year from the date on which the order or judgment was pronounced, or (b) 3 months from the coming into force of these rules, whichever occurs first.

data.text:

data.title: Time runs different from event
data.text:
Where the time limit provided by these rules for doing anything runs from a different event than the equivalent time limit under the former rules, and on the coming into force of these rules the thing has not yet been done, the time limit provided by these rules applies, calculated either (a) from the event specified in these rules, or (b) from the coming into force of these rules, whichever occurs later.

data.title: Formal offer to settle
data.text:
A formal offer to settle an existing proceeding that was made and neither withdrawn nor accepted prior to the coming into force of these rules remains open for acceptance in accordance with the former rules.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 15.11 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*

data.title: New test or criteria
data.text:
Where these rules impose a new test, provide new criteria or provide an additional ground for making an application in an existing proceeding, these rules apply in respect of the application if the application was made but has not been heard prior to the coming into force of these rules.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 15.12 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*

data.title: Place of existing proceeding
data.text:
The coming into force of rules 3.3 and 3.4 does not operate to require an existing proceeding to be carried on in a different judicial centre from the judicial centre in which it was commenced.
